acceptanceCriteria: A governing row whose content contains zero-width, bidi-control or tag characters carries a named warning and is downgraded from authoritative, covered by fixtures.
A governing file changed in the diff under review is reported as self-modified authority in the packet and in cem status, not cited as authority for hunks in the same change.
The threat is recorded in docs with the two external references.
body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). Instruction files are a known injection path: the Rules File Backdoor hid instructions in invisible Unicode (pillar.security), and AGENTS.md injection exfiltrated credentials in Codex (backslash.security). Corvint elevates AGENTS.md, specs and decisions to top authority, so a poisoned governing file inherits that authority. No invisible or bidi character screening was found in internal/contextindex. A second gap: a governing file modified in the working tree or in the change under review (an agent granting itself authority) is not distinguished from committed authority in the packet or the CEM.
title: security: flag hidden or bidirectional Unicode in governing documents and governing files changed in the same diff
